Q1124.label: Bill Clinton
Q1124.summary: William Jefferson Clinton is an American retired politician and lawyer who served as the 42nd president of the United States from 1993 to 2001. A member of the Democratic Party, he previously served as the attorney general of Arkansas from 1977 to 1979, the governor of Arkansas from 1979 to 1981, and governor again from 1983 to 1992.

Q2255460.label: 2006 Haitian general election
Q2255460.desc: General elections held in Haiti on 7 February 2006
Q2255460.summary: General elections were held in Haiti on 7 February 2006 to elect the replacements for the interim government of Gérard Latortue, which had been put in place after the 2004 Haiti rebellion. The elections were delayed four times, having originally been scheduled for October and November 2005.

Q931428.label: 1977 Irish general election
Q931428.summary: The 1977 Irish general election to the 21st Dáil was held on Thursday, 16 June, following the dissolution of the 20th Dáil on 25 May by President Patrick Hillery on the request of Taoiseach Liam Cosgrave. The general election took place in 42 Dáil constituencies throughout Ireland for 148 seats in Dáil Éireann, the house of representatives of the Oireachtas, an increase of four seats. There was a significant revision of constituencies under the Electoral (Amendment) Act 1974. Jack Lynch led Fianna Fáil to a landslide election win, clearly defeating the outgoing Fine Gael–Labour government.

Q7857764.label: Twenty-third Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q7857764.desc: To permit the state to become a party to the International Criminal Court
aliases: 23rd Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q7857764.wiki: Twenty-third Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q7857764.summary: The Twenty-third Amendment of the Constitution Act 2001 of the Constitution of Ireland is an amendment that permitted the state to become a party to the International Criminal Court (ICC). It was approved by referendum on 7 June 2001 and signed into law on the 27 March 2002.

Q124488292.desc: Hungarian lawyer and politician, Prime Minister of Hungary since 2026
Q124488292.summary: Péter Magyar is a Hungarian politician who has served as prime minister of Hungary since May 2026. He has been the president of the Tisza Party since 2024 and was a member of the European Parliament (MEP) from 2024 to 2026.

Q1783396.label: 1946 Italian general election
Q1783396.summary: General elections were held in Italy on Sunday 2 and also on Monday 3 June 1946. They were the first after World War II and elected 556 deputies to the Constituent Assembly. Theoretically, a total of 573 deputies were to be elected, but the election did not take place in the Julian March and in South Tyrol, which were under military occupation by the United Nations.

Q983140.label: George Borg Olivier
Q983140.img: Statue Giorgio Borg Olivier Castille Square Valletta n2.jpg
Q983140.summary: Giorgio Borg Olivier was a Maltese politician. He twice served as Prime Minister of Malta and as the Leader of the Nationalist Party. He was also Leader of the Opposition between 1955–1958, and again between 1971–1977.

Positions held: Member of the House of Representatives of Malta

Q366692.img: Mesut Yilmaz as Turkish Prime Minister.jpg

Q911972.label: Dunkirk evacuation
Q911972.desc: evacuation of Allied soldiers from the beaches and harbour of Dunkirk, France, between 27 May and 4 June 1940
Q911972.summary: In the Dunkirk evacuation, codenamed Operation Dynamo and also known as the Miracle of Dunkirk, or just Dunkirk, more than 338,000 Allied soldiers were evacuated during the Second World War from the beaches and harbour of Dunkirk in northern France between 26 May and 4 June 1940. The operation began after large numbers of Belgian, British, and French troops were cut off and surrounded by German troops during the six-week Battle of France.

Q86675044.label: Bombing of Genoa in World War II
Q86675044.desc: WWII bombardment against Italian industrial city Genoa
Q86675044.wiki: Bombing of Genoa in World War II
Q86675044.summary: Owing to the importance of its port and industries, the Italian port city of Genoa, the regional capital and largest city of Liguria, was heavily bombarded by both Allied air and naval forces during Second World War, suffering heavy damage.

Q3575908.label: Zone interdite
Q3575908.desc: German occupation zone in France during WW2
Q3575908.summary: The zone interdite was an administrative area in German–occupied France during World War II along the country's Atlantic coast from Spain to Belgium.

Q2363492.label: Battle of El Guettar
Q2363492.img: American soldiers hands out cigarettes to captured Italians of the Bersaglieri Division near El Guettar, Tunisia. - NARA - 196343.jpg
Q2363492.summary: The Battle of El Guettar took place from 23 March – 3 April 1943, in south-central Tunisia during the Tunisia Campaign of World War II. It was fought by elements of the Army Group Africa under General Hans-Jürgen von Arnim, along with Italian First Army under General Giovanni Messe, against the U.S. II Corps under Lieutenant General George Patton. It was the first battle in which U.S. forces were able to defeat the experienced Italian and German tank units, but the followup to the battle was inconclusive.

Q550500.label: Battle of Nam Dong
Q550500.summary: The battle of Nam Đông took place from July 5–6, 1964 during the Vietnam War, when the Viet Cong (VC) and People's Army of Vietnam (PAVN) attacked the Nam Đông CIDG camp in an attempt to overrun it. During the battle, 57 South Vietnamese defenders, two Americans, an Australian military advisor, and at least 62 attackers were killed.

Q208484.label: Lebanese Civil War
Q208484.summary: The Lebanese Civil War was a multifaceted armed conflict fought in Lebanon from 1975 to 1990. It resulted in an estimated 120,000 deaths, displaced nearly one million people, and caused widespread destruction across the country.

Participants: United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon

mentions.c: Month by month, 1975–1990: 31 battles and operations, 144,011 battle deaths

Q3354724.label: Operation Hoover
Q3354724.summary: Operation Hoover was a 2007 Canadian-led offensive in the War in Afghanistan against the Taliban in the Kandahar Province district of Zhari. The aims of the operation were to root out as many as 300 suspected Afghan insurgents who had moved into the villages of the Zhari District. Operation Hoover was initially an H Company/A Squadron Combat Team operation, but grew to a 2nd Battalion Royal Canadian Regiment Battle Group operation for the final phase in Nalgham, Zhari. Operation Hoover was part of the overarching Operation Baaz Tsuka.

Q4872292.label: Battle of Sangin
Q4872292.summary: The Battle for Sangin was an extended campaign during the War in Afghanistan. Sangin is considered the bloodiest battleground of Afghanistan by both the United States and United Kingdom alike. With both nations suffering the loss of over 100 killed in action, and several hundred moderate to severe casualties.

Q135208548.label: Al-Baqa Cafe airstrike
Q135208548.desc: airstrike by Israeli Air Force, possible war crime
Q135208548.summary: On 30 June 2025, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) conducted an airstrike on the al-Baqa internet café near the port of Gaza City, within the Gaza Strip. The attack killed at least 41 people—including photojournalist Ismail Abu Hatab—and injured another 75. Reportedly, most of the casualties were women and children.

Q191076.label: Bose-Einstein statistics
Q191076.desc: statistical description for the behaviour of bosons
Q191076.summary: In quantum statistics, Bose–Einstein statistics describes one of two possible ways in which a collection of non-interacting identical particles may occupy a set of available discrete energy states at thermodynamic equilibrium. The aggregation of particles in the same state, which is a characteristic of particles obeying Bose–Einstein statistics, accounts for the cohesive streaming of laser light and the frictionless creeping of superfluid helium.

Q28647524.label: Reactive Scientific Research Institute
Q28647524.summary: Reactive Scientific Research Institute was one of the first Soviet research and development institutions to focus on rocket technology. RNII developed the Katyusha rocket launcher and its research and development were very important for later achievements of the Soviet rocket and space programs.

mentions.c: Gagarin, the first human in space (1961)

Q273508.label: cosmic inflation
Q273508.desc: cosmological model that fits within the Big Bang paradigm, according to which a region of the universe—including the observable universe—underwent a phase of very rapid expansion that is thought to have caused it to grow by a considerable factor
Q273508.summary: In physical cosmology, cosmic inflation, cosmological inflation, or just inflation, is a theory of exponential expansion of space in the very early universe. This enormous expansion supercooled the universe and ended when the energy content of the field driving inflation condensed into hot, dense particles, a process called reheating. Following the inflationary period, the universe continued to expand, but at a slower rate.

Q49764.label: Die Linke
Q49764.summary: Die Linke, also known as the Left Party, is a democratic socialist political party in Germany. The party was founded in 2007 as the result of the merger of the Party of Democratic Socialism (PDS) and Labour and Social Justice – The Electoral Alternative. Through the PDS, the party is the direct descendant of the Marxist–Leninist ruling party of former East Germany, the Socialist Unity Party of Germany (SED). Since June 2026, Die Linke's co-chairpersons have been Ines Schwerdtner and Luigi Pantisano.

Q1274468.label: Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina
Q1274468.desc: official-name and constitutional period of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1992 to 1995
Q1274468.summary: The Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was the Bosnian state in Southeastern Europe, existing from 1992 to 1995. It is the direct legal predecessor to the modern-day federal republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
